intro: When you search for an architect near you, you likely have a building project in mind — perhaps a home extension, a renovation, or a new build — and you want a local professional who understands your area and can guide you through the process. We introduce you to architects in the UK who can quote for your work, so you can compare approaches and fees directly.
need_heading: What people searching for an architect near me usually need
need_lead: Most people looking for an architect near them are at the start of a building project and need local, professional help to turn their ideas into reality.
needs: You own a house and want to extend it, but you need drawings and planning permission before you can begin.
You are planning a loft conversion or a garage conversion and need to know whether it is feasible and what permissions are required.
You have bought a property that needs major renovation and want an architect to help you reconfigure the layout and oversee the work.
You are considering a self-build project and need an architect to design a new home that suits your plot and budget.
You want to alter a listed building or a property in a conservation area and need an architect who understands the extra constraints.
context_heading: What you should know about hiring an architect near you
context: In the UK, the title 'architect' is protected by law. Only people on the Architects Registration Board (ARB) register can call themselves architects, and they must follow the ARB code of conduct and hold professional indemnity insurance. Many practices are also RIBA Chartered Practices. Architectural designers and technologists can do excellent work too, but they are not registered architects, so it is worth knowing which you are hiring.

Before you appoint anyone, check the ARB register and ask for a written appointment that sets out services, fees and responsibilities. Building regulations approval, planning permission and party wall matters are separate processes that your architect can help you navigate.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Describe the type of building project you are planning, such as an extension, renovation, or new build.
Mention the location of the property so we can introduce you to an architect familiar with your area.
Explain whether you already have planning permission or need help with the planning application.
Let us know if your property is listed or in a conservation area, as this affects the design approach.
Share your rough budget range so the architect can tailor their quote appropriately.
Indicate your preferred timeline, such as when you hope to start on site.
questions: Are you registered with the Architects Registration Board?
What experience do you have with projects similar to mine, especially in this local area?
How will you charge for your services, and what is included in your fee?
Will you handle the planning application and building regulations approval on my behalf?
Can you provide a written appointment that clearly sets out the scope of work and responsibilities?
How will you keep me informed and involved throughout the design and construction process?

faqs.q: Do I need an architect for my project?
faqs.a: Not every project legally requires an architect, but for many building projects an architect can add real value by designing a scheme that meets your needs and guiding you through planning and building regulations. If your project is complex or you want professional design input, an architect is a wise choice.

faqs.q: What is the difference between an architect and an architectural designer?
faqs.a: An architect is a protected title in the UK, meaning only those on the Architects Registration Board register can use it. Architectural designers can also design buildings and prepare drawings, but they are not regulated in the same way, so it is important to check which you are hiring.

faqs.q: How do I check if someone is a registered architect?
faqs.a: You can check the Architects Registration Board (ARB) register online or by contacting the ARB directly. It is a quick and free way to confirm that the person you are considering is a registered architect.

faqs.q: Will my architect handle planning permission for me?
faqs.a: Many architects offer planning application services as part of their work, but you should confirm this in your written appointment. Planning permission is a separate process, and your architect can prepare and submit the application on your behalf.

extra_heading: Narrowing down architects close to you
extra: Searching for an architect near me suggests you want someone who can visit the site without a long journey, and that is a practical starting point. A local architect will already know your planning authority's habits and the kinds of properties typical of your area, which can save time when drawings and applications are prepared. Distance is not everything, though, so weigh it alongside the experience that matters for your project.

When you compare the architects we introduce you to, ask each one how they would approach your particular building and what they have done on similar properties nearby. Because quotes are price on application, ask what the fee covers and whether it is fixed or charged in stages, so you can compare like with like rather than headline figures. A short conversation with each practice usually tells you more than any description.

At a first appointment, expect to walk the site together and talk through what you hope to achieve, your rough budget and any constraints such as listed status or a tight plot. The architect should explain what permissions are likely to be needed and how their work would be set out in a written appointment, often using RIBA stages. You do not have to decide on the day, and it is sensible to speak to more than one before appointing anyone.

extra_faqs.q: Does an architect near me need to visit the property before quoting?
extra_faqs.a: Many architects will want to see the site or at least discuss it in detail before giving a firm quote, because the condition of the building and the plot affect the work involved. A first visit is also your chance to judge whether you would work well together.

extra_faqs.q: Can I use an architect who is not based in my town?
extra_faqs.a: Yes. What matters most is that they can visit your property and are familiar with your local planning authority, which may be some distance from their office. Convenience for site visits is worth weighing, but relevant experience counts too.
